newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds close much higher in thin market.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds close much higher in thin market.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished much higher Thursday after a session in which very thin trading volumes exaggerated the upward move.
"The market is continuing its strong trend," said a trader at an Argentine bank. "I don't see big obstacles for the market up ahead."
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.80 at 123.30, while the FRB due 2005 rose 1/4 to 87.
Trade was slim but the strong tone that has dominated during all of December sufficed to push prices higher despite a general strike protesting the government's labor reforms Thursday.

Traders said the market's prospects for the beginning of the New Year were looking increasingly positive, particularly as global interest rates were likely to remain low in the coming year, meaning investors would continue to seek higher yields like those found in emerging markets.
"While the interest rate cycle has only turned in one G-10 country, the U.K., the biggest risk for the Brady market as usual rests with the U.S.," said financial consultants IDEA in an investor note.
In the money market, call money rates rose to 7.38 percent from 6.65 percent.
